item.title: Implement spec-complete safe_extract with focused tests
item.brief: Implement safe_extract.py according to SPEC.md, preserving extract(entries, root) API. Cover every specified validation rule and boundary/error case, with focused additions to test_safe_extract.py. Use only Python standard library. Ensure the full batch and root/target tree are validated before any mutation; validation failures leave root/outside unchanged, and unexpected I/O errors remain visible. Run the test suite and any focused checks. Commit the completed work on the item branch; the registered repo ships local. Acceptance criteria: all existing and new tests pass; malformed batch/data/path, duplicate and file-directory collisions, invalid root/symlink/non-directory ancestors/existing targets are rejected with ValueError; empty batch validates root; nested valid entries preserve order and exact bytes including empty files.

pr.body: Implemented the existing `extract(entries, root)` API using only the Python standard library. Root path spelling is normalized only after rejecting the empty string, so trailing separators cannot bypass root symlink checks and an empty root cannot become the current directory. Added focused tests for batch/data/path validation, duplicate and file-directory collisions, existing filesystem conflicts, symlinks, invalid roots, literal percent signs, output order, and empty files. Full available suite: `python -m unittest -v` (9 passed); `git diff --check` passed. Assumption: the caller provides a stable filesystem as specified; concurrent changes and rollback after I/O errors remain out of scope.
pr.summary: Safe extraction now validates every entry and destination before writing. It rejects malformed batches, unsafe paths, collisions, symlink roots and components, and existing targets; valid nested files preserve order and exact bytes.
pr.title: Implement safe extraction validation

risk.why: Contained behavior change to the existing extraction API in safe_extract.py with focused coverage in test_safe_extract.py. The initial implementation had a root-symlink spelling bypass, found by all three whole-change reviewers and fixed; a focused follow-up found empty-root normalization, also fixed. Final full suite and final focused review pass.
